results.name: shared_last_digit_far
results.description: For targets more than 15 outside the examples' range, yes-rate when the target shares its last digit with some example minus when it shares none; observed < null means the model over-generalises by "ends in d" rules relative to people, observed > null means people use last-digit similarity more.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_far
# description: For targets more than 15 outside the examples' range, yes-rate when the target shares its last digit with some example minus when it shares none; observed < null means the model over-generalises by "ends in d" rules relative to people, observed > null means people use last-digit similarity more.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    P = parts.values
    lo = np.nanmin(P, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(P, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    gap = np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi)
    far = gap > 15
    share = np.nansum((np.mod(P, 10) == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None]), axis=1) > 0
    y = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a, b = far & share, far & ~share
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: small_minus_large_set_extension
results.description: Yes-rate for targets 1-15 outside the examples' range in sets whose max <= 40 minus that in sets whose min >= 55; observed > null means people extend small-number sets more (relative to large-number sets) than the model's power-law endpoint prior predicts, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: small_minus_large_set_extension
# description: Yes-rate for targets 1-15 outside the examples' range in sets whose max <= 40 minus that in sets whose min >= 55; observed > null means people extend small-number sets more (relative to large-number sets) than the model's power-law endpoint prior predicts, observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    lo = parts.min(axis=1).values
    hi = parts.max(axis=1).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    gap = np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi)
    out = (gap >= 1) & (gap <= 15)
    y = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a, b = out & (hi <= 40), out & (lo >= 55)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: primacy_first_minus_last_near
results.description: In multi-example sets, yes-rate for non-example targets within 6 of the first-shown example (and >6 from all others) minus that for targets within 6 of the last-shown example only; observed > null means people weight the first example more than the sticky-first-guess model, observed < null means the model overstates primacy.
results.code:
# name: primacy_first_minus_last_near
# description: In multi-example sets, yes-rate for non-example targets within 6 of the first-shown example (and >6 from all others) minus that for targets within 6 of the last-shown example only; observed > null means people weight the first example more than the sticky-first-guess model, observed < null means the model overstates primacy.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    n = parts.notna().sum(axis=1).values
    P = parts.values
    first = P[:, 0]
    last = P[np.arange(len(P)), n - 1]
    dist = np.abs(P - t[:, None])
    isex = np.nansum(dist == 0, axis=1) > 0
    near = np.where(np.isnan(dist), False, dist <= 6)
    cnt = near.sum(axis=1)
    near_first = (np.abs(first - t) <= 6) & (cnt == 1)
    near_last = (np.abs(last - t) <= 6) & (cnt == 1)
    ok = (n >= 2) & ~isex
    y = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a, b = ok & near_first, ok & near_last
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: single_example_mid_distance_yes
results.description: Yes-rate among one-example sets for targets 15-50 away from the example; observed < null means people generalise less to moderately distant numbers from a lone example than the model's range/rule guesses imply, observed > null means more.
results.code:
# name: single_example_mid_distance_yes
# description: Yes-rate among one-example sets for targets 15-50 away from the example; observed < null means people generalise less to moderately distant numbers from a lone example than the model's range/rule guesses imply, observed > null means more.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",")
    x = pd.to_numeric(s.where(single, "0"), errors="coerce").fillna(0).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    d = np.abs(t - x)
    m = single.values & (d >= 15) & (d <= 50)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())

results.name: below_minus_above_near
results.description: Yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the set minimum minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the set maximum (multi-example sets); observed < null means people extend upward relatively more (downward less) than the model predicts, observed > null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: below_minus_above_near
# description: Yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the set minimum minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the set maximum (multi-example sets); observed < null means people extend upward relatively more (downward less) than the model predicts, observed > null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    n = parts.notna().sum(axis=1).values
    lo = parts.min(axis=1).values
    hi = parts.max(axis=1).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    y = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    below = (n >= 2) & (lo - t >= 1) & (lo - t <= 10)
    above = (n >= 2) & (t - hi >= 1) & (t - hi <= 10)
    if below.sum() == 0 or above.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[below].mean() - y[above].mean())

results.name: adjacent_neighbour_yes
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets 1-3 away from some example in multi-example sets; observed < null means people endorse immediate numerical neighbours of examples less than the model (whose range guesses nearly always cover them), observed > null means more.
results.code:
# name: adjacent_neighbour_yes
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets 1-3 away from some example in multi-example sets; observed < null means people endorse immediate numerical neighbours of examples less than the model (whose range guesses nearly always cover them), observed > null means more.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    P = parts.values
    n = parts.notna().sum(axis=1).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(P - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & (d >= 1) & (d <= 3)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())

results.name: cluster_interior_yes
results.description: For 3-4-example sets spanning <= 40, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' range; observed < null means people fill in a compact cluster's interior less than the model's range guesses predict, observed > null means more.
results.code:
# name: cluster_interior_yes
# description: For 3-4-example sets spanning <= 40, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' range; observed < null means people fill in a compact cluster's interior less than the model's range guesses predict, observed > null means more.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    P = parts.values
    n = parts.notna().sum(axis=1).values
    lo = np.nanmin(P, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(P, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    isex = np.nansum(P == t[:, None], axis=1) > 0
    m = (n >= 3) & (hi - lo <= 40) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~isex
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())

results.name: inrange_four_minus_two
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' range in 4-example sets minus in 2-example sets; observed > null means more examples raise in-range filling more for people than in the model (stronger evidence for a range), observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: inrange_four_minus_two
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the examples' range in 4-example sets minus in 2-example sets; observed > null means more examples raise in-range filling more for people than in the model (stronger evidence for a range), observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    P = parts.values
    n = parts.notna().sum(axis=1).values
    lo = np.nanmin(P, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(P, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    isex = np.nansum(P == t[:, None], axis=1) > 0
    inr = (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~isex
    y = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a, b = inr & (n == 4), inr & (n == 2)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())
